name: Y Combinator (Winter 2027 batch; Spring 2027 next)
what: 3-month startup accelerator for founders, with seed investment and Demo Day.
value: YC standard investment + program (see YC site for current terms)
why: BioBridge (30k users) plus her AI-agent build make a credible solo-founder application.
notes: W27 deadline is 8pm PT; YC still reviews late applications. Spring 2027 deadline not announced yet (Spring 2026's was Feb 9). Early Decision for later batches also exists.

name: Tory Burch Foundation Fellows Program (2027 cohort)
what: Year-long program for US women entrepreneurs: workshop week, peer network, and access to capital.
value: Program + network; some listings mention a $5,000 grant (sources conflict)
why: Women-founder program that fits BioBridge as an operating US business.
notes: Third-party sources; one gives 2026-11-02 instead. Requires age 21+ and a US-formed, US-operating business. Check the official site.

name: Tarbell Fellowship 2027–28
what: Paid one-year AI journalism fellowship: 3-month training, a summit, then a 9-month newsroom placement (past hosts: TIME, The Verge, MIT Tech Review).
value: Salary reported at $75,000–$120,000; summit travel covered
why: Turns her science-creator and AI-explainer skills into a credentialed AI-reporting role starting June 2027, after she graduates.
notes: Deadline from several third-party listings for the 2027–28 cohort (June 2027–May 2028). One older listing showed a January deadline for a previous cohort. Verify on tarbellcenter.org. Tarbell also offers $1k–$20k AI reporting grants (tarbellcenter.org/grants).

name: Science Ambassador Scholarship 2027
what: Full-tuition-style award for women and non-binary STEM students, judged on a 3-minute public YouTube mini-lecture.
value: Five $20,000 tuition scholarships
why: A video science lecture is exactly what she makes for 85k followers; strong edge as a creator.
notes: Aggregators give Dec 14–16, 2026; confirm on official site. Undergrads eligible. Tuition is for the 2027 academic year, so check that her MS year counts.

name: Hult Prize 2027
what: Global student social-impact startup competition: campus rounds, then regionals, then a global final.
value: US$1,000,000 grand prize
why: BioBridge's education mission fits an impact-startup pitch, and she can lead a 3–4-person team.
notes: Deadline is from a third-party aggregator; past cycles closed early to mid February. Confirm with hultprize.org or a Jefferson campus organizer.

name: Global Student Entrepreneur Awards (GSEA)
what: Competition for students who already own and run a business: local, then national, then global finals.
deadline: Varies by region (US local deadlines are often early Dec; e.g., Dec 5 in a 2025–26 US cycle)
value: Global finals prize pool US$100,000 (1st place $50,000); local prizes vary; no participation costs
why: Built for student founders with a running business, which BioBridge is.
notes: Requires age 18–30, active enrollment, a business running 6+ months, and $500+ revenue or $1,000+ investment. Contact EO Philadelphia for the local date.

name: AAAS Mass Media Science & Engineering Fellowship (Summer 2027)
organizer: American Association for the Advancement of Science
what: 10-week summer placement as a science reporter at a major media outlet.
value: $10,000 stipend + travel
why: Prestigious sci-comm credential that turns her creator work into newsroom experience; upper-level undergrads qualify.
notes: Confirmed on the AAAS program page. Requires US citizenship or a visa allowing paid summer work, plus a writing sample for a lay audience.

name: NCAA Postgraduate Scholarship (fall sports)
what: Award for student-athletes in their final season who excel in academics, athletics and leadership, put toward graduate study.
value: $7,000 one-time
why: D-II runner with a 3.75 GPA and founder leadership; it could fund her MS year.
notes: Fall window (cross country): Sept 15, 2026 to Jan 5, 2027, 5pm ET. Her Faculty Athletics Rep must nominate her, so ask about the internal deadline now. Track athletes use the winter/spring windows (2027-03-09 / 2027-05-04). She must have finished her final season of competition.

name: National CLARION Interprofessional Case Competition 2027
organizer: University of Minnesota Center for Health Interprofessional Programs
what: National interdisciplinary healthcare case competition; teams of up to 4 students.
value: National competition exposure; team fee $2,000 early-bird (to Nov 13) / $2,250
why: Jefferson's health-sciences mix suits interprofessional teams, and it shows off her biotech-plus-analytics profile.
notes: Competition Apr 9–10, 2027. Aimed at health-professions students and usually entered through a school's local round, so check whether Jefferson participates.

name: Kleiner Perkins Fellows 2027
what: Summer fellowship at a KP portfolio startup in the Bay Area, with founder talks and a community.
value: Paid summer role at a portfolio company + KP network
why: A top VC talent network, and her AI-agent build and VC database show technical and venture interest.
notes: 2027 tracks listed are Engineering and Design (both fairly technical). Rolling review, so apply early. Deadline is 11:59pm PST Jan 31, per Harvard career listing.

name: Claude Corps Fellowship (Jan & Aug 2027 cohorts)
what: One-year paid fellowship placing early-career people at nonprofits to help them adopt AI (Claude).
value: $85,000 salary + benefits + Claude API/tooling
why: The August 2027 cohort starts right after her May graduation and builds on her Anthropic brand work and Pfizer AI-agent experience.
notes: Requires under 2 years of full-time experience. Reportedly you must finish Anthropic's AI Fluency and Claude 101 courses before applying. Rolling review, so earlier is better.

name: Rice Business Plan Competition 2027
what: Large intercollegiate student startup competition with a Life Science & Healthcare track.
value: Large cash and investment prize pool (2027 amounts not yet published)
why: A biotech/edtech venture pitch on a national stage in front of investors.
notes: Needs 2+ student founders, with at least one in a graduate program. Her BS/MS status may qualify, but confirm. In 2025, past equity raised was capped at $250k.

name: Cursor Campus Leads (Spring cohort)
what: Campus ambassadors run workshops, hackathons and meetups for Cursor.
value: Expenses-paid SF office trip, 6 months of Cursor Ultra, one hackathon trip reimbursed, swag
why: Her BizBio Club and audience let her run AI-building events and add another AI-company partnership.
notes: Runs fall and spring cohorts, about 5 hrs/week, for current students. Cursor's page says applications reopen in January.

name: Webby Awards (31st Annual)
organizer: International Academy of Digital Arts & Sciences
what: Major internet awards with Creator, Video, Social and AI categories.
deadline: TBD (30th cycle: early Oct 24, 2025; final Feb 6, 2026)
value: Award and honoree recognition; entry fees apply
why: A Webby or honoree nod for her science content or BioBridge would boost her creator credentials.
notes: 31st-cycle dates were not found in search; a late-2026 to early-2027 final deadline is likely but unconfirmed.

name: TreeHacks 2027
what: Selective 36-hour hackathon at Stanford with large sponsor prizes (2026 awarded about $500k).
value: Travel/lodging support often offered; sponsor prizes
why: High-signal AI-builder event; she could build a biotech AI-agent project with sponsor AI labs she already knows.
notes: About 1,000 of 15,000 applicants were accepted in 2026. Event dates come from a third-party roundup; check treehacks.com for when applications open.

name: South Park Commons Founder Fellowship (Spring 2027)
what: Bootcamp and residency for founders exploring 'from -1 to 0', in SF/NYC.
value: $400k for 7% (SAFE) + $600k guaranteed in next round; $900k+ in credits
why: Strong option if she wants to go full-time on a biotech/AI company after graduation.
notes: Full-time availability at an SPC office is required. Spring 2026 bootcamp ran late March to late May; check for the Spring/Fall 2027 call.

name: 2048 Ventures VC Fellowship (Bio track)
what: Part-time pre-seed VC fellowship with Vertical AI, Deep Tech, Health and Bio tracks.
value: Hands-on deal exposure, access to the investment team, possible path into VC
why: Direct biotech-VC experience that builds on her 130+ firm database.
notes: Asks for a 2–5 min intro video. No Spring 2027 cohort confirmed yet.

name: MIT Hacking Medicine GrandHack 2027
what: In-person healthcare hackathon at MIT with clinicians, engineers and entrepreneurs.
deadline: TBD (2026 deadline was Feb 15 for a Mar 13–15 event)
value: Prizes and sponsor exposure (amounts vary)
why: Healthcare/biotech hackathon where her regulatory-AI agent experience stands out.
notes: 2027 edition not yet announced. Contact grandhack@mit.edu.

name: Wharton Health Care Business Conference 2027
what: Large student-run healthcare business conference with pharma, biotech and investor speakers.
value: Discounted full-time student tickets (non-Wharton students have emailed info@whcbc.org for the student rate)
why: In Philadelphia, a networking hub for biotech investors and pharma leaders.
notes: Feb 18–19, 2027 at the Union League of Philadelphia, per a third-party listing; confirm on the official site.

name: Wharton Undergraduate Healthcare Conference 2027
what: Self-described largest undergraduate healthcare conference in the US, with a career fair.
deadline: TBD (historically late Jan / Feb at the Inn at Penn)
value: Low-cost student tickets; career fair access
why: Nearby in Philly, with recruiters and a chance to promote BizBio Club and BioBridge.
notes: 2025 edition was Jan 25 and open to all attendees. 2027 date not yet published.

name: 2027 Women Redefining Entrepreneurship Scholarship
what: Essay scholarship for women college and graduate students interested in entrepreneurship.
why: Easy win for a woman founder with a 3.75 GPA.
notes: Requires a 3.0+ GPA and a 750–1,000 word essay. Listing is from Fastweb; confirm with the sponsor.

name: AWIS Undergraduate Scholarships (2027 cycle)
what: National scholarships for undergraduate women in science.
deadline: Opens early 2027 (2025 and 2026 deadlines were Feb 28)
value: Up to about $2,500 (2026 figure)
why: Women-in-STEM award for a biotech major with a strong outreach record; AWIS also has a Philadelphia chapter (awisphl.org).
notes: 2026 cycle closed; sign up on AWIS for the 2027 opening. Read the eligibility details, since some awards are field-specific.

name: SynBioBeta Student Grant
what: Student package to attend SynBioBeta, the leading synthetic-biology and bioeconomy conference.
deadline: TBD (historically late March; 2024 deadline was Mar 29)
value: Conference attendance benefits package
why: Puts her among synbio founders and biotech VCs; a source of content and deals for BioBridge.
notes: 2027 program not confirmed. Past conferences also held a Students + Early-Stage Founders luncheon.

name: BIO International Convention 2027 – Student Program
what: Free student passes to the world's largest biotech convention.
value: Free convention entry (otherwise expensive)
why: BIO 2027 is in Philadelphia, her home city: a must-attend for biotech VC networking and content.
notes: Limited passes, accepted on a rolling basis. Needs a .edu email and student ID. Travel/lodging is on the student. Contact studentprogram@bio.org.

name: Paragon Policy Fellowship
what: Part-time remote program where students do tech-policy projects for state and local governments.
value: Summer 2026 was unpaid; earlier cycles paid a $500 stipend
why: Low-barrier AI/biotech policy credential for a non-CS student.
notes: About 8–10 hrs/week. No 2027 call found yet; applications historically open 1–2 months before each cohort.

name: Open Sauce NextUp
what: Free 6-month accelerator for emerging STEM and maker creators: mentorship, equipment and an LA trip.
value: Mentorship, equipment, LA trip, creator community
why: Science-creator growth program from the Open Sauce/YouTube STEM community.
notes: Requires 18+, US resident, and under 100,000 YouTube subscribers. Check her YouTube count specifically. The next cycle is not yet announced.

name: VCIC – Venture Capital Investment Competition (Undergraduate)
what: Students act as VCs, evaluating real startups and pitching term sheets; campus, regional and global rounds.
deadline: Via school (campus teams usually form in fall; finals in spring)
value: Judged by real VCs; strong VC-recruiting signal
why: Directly tests the VC skills behind her 130-firm database and BizBio Club.
notes: One 5-person undergraduate team per school. Jefferson must take part, or she could ask her business school about entering.

name: Emergent Ventures
what: Fast, low-friction grants and fellowships for ambitious individuals and projects.
value: Grant amount varies by project
why: Fits a young founder-creator with a concrete project (e.g., scaling BioBridge or biotech-VC research).
notes: Short proposal (≤1,500 words), and Cowen reads every application. Rolling status was inferred from responses arriving within about a week.

name: Thiel Fellowship
what: Two-year grant for young people to build instead of attending college.
value: Six-figure grant (third-party sources list $100k–$250k; verify)
why: Only relevant if she is 22 or under and willing to go all-in on BioBridge.
notes: HARD LIMITS: age 22 or under, and she must leave school to accept. Check her age. Graduating in May 2027 conflicts with the leave-school requirement.

name: Z Fellows
what: One-week mostly virtual sprint for about 10 builders, ending with an in-person day in SF or NYC.
value: Optional $10,000 investment at a $1B cap + network
why: Low-cost founder credential and network for BioBridge or a new AI-bio project.
notes: Cohorts roughly every other month. Optional 1-minute founder video.

name: 1517 Medici Grant
what: No-strings micro-grants for students pursuing ambitious side projects.
why: Quick funding for a BioBridge feature or a content series, and a door into 1517's network.
notes: Short form with links to demos or docs. Details come from third-party listings; confirm on 1517fund.com.

name: a16z speedrun (SR008)
what: a16z's early-stage accelerator (SR008 reportedly runs late Jan to Apr 2027 in SF).
value: a16z investment + program (see site for current terms)
why: Top-tier VC accelerator that values consumer, AI and creator-led startups like BioBridge.
notes: SR007 closed 2026-05-17. a16z TxO is paused, so don't target it.

name: Sloan Foundation – YouTube & TikTok Science Grants
organizer: Alfred P. Sloan Foundation (Public Understanding of Science)
what: Grants for accurate science and tech content on YouTube and TikTok aimed at young audiences.
value: Grant size varies (project-based)
why: Funding built for exactly her format: science explainers for a young social audience.
notes: Email a one-page letter of inquiry to VP/Program Director Doron Weber. Response takes up to 8 weeks; full proposals are by invite only. Excludes K-12 study aids.

name: Amber Grant for Women
what: Monthly grants for women-owned businesses.
deadline: Rolling (monthly cutoffs, end of each month)
value: $10,000 monthly awards; monthly winners can compete for year-end $50,000 grants
why: Non-dilutive cash for BioBridge as a woman-owned business.
notes: Some months are limited to one industry. Small application fee applies; check current terms.

name: BlueDot Impact AI courses (incl. AI Governance)
what: Free cohort-based AI safety and governance courses, the common entry point to AI policy fellowships.
value: Free; certificate and network
why: Fast way for a non-CS student to build AI-policy credentials before applying to IAPS, GovAI or Horizon in summer 2027.
notes: Course formats change; check bluedot.org for current cohorts.
